criteria.quote: Moltres may heal injuries by burning in magma.
criteria.revision: Open with: "Moltres controls fire. So why does its injury remedy involve molten magma?" Then reveal the healing claim afterward.

criteria.quote: Moltres is said to heal injuries by dipping its body into a volcano's molten magma.
Why would a fire-controlling bird use molten magma to heal?
criteria.revision: Make the uncertainty more evidence-grounded: "If Moltres is injured, why does the Pokédex say it dips its body into molten magma to burn and heal itself?"

criteria.quote: The entry's sequence is simple: injured first, then dipped into molten magma.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated injury beats with a progression: establish that Moltres controls fire, reveal that every wing flap creates flames or embers, then reveal the separate claim that injury leads it to dip into molten magma.

criteria.quote: The same fire Moltres controls becomes the answer when injury strikes.
criteria.revision: Create the reveal by delaying the magma detail: first establish fire control, then say, "But when injured, it is said to dip its body into molten magma to burn and heal itself."

criteria.quote: Moltres may heal injuries by burning in magma.
criteria.revision: Remove the repeated magma descriptions and use distinct documented details: its wings create flames or scatter embers, it is said to bring spring, and its flame-cloaked wings have been said to light paths for people lost in the mountains.

criteria.quote: The same fire Moltres controls becomes the answer when injury strikes.
criteria.revision: Do not claim the research explains why. End with: "The Pokédex never explains why—it only says that when injured, Moltres is said to dip its body into volcanic magma to burn and heal itself."

criteria.quote: Would you trust magma healing, or call it too dangerous?
criteria.revision: Use the research's uncertainty for a sharper split: "Is Moltres's magma healing a real ability—or only a claim the Pokédex says is 'said' to happen?"
